title: Keritot 15
description: Names and bodies: whether Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri and Sumakhos really said the same thing, Rabbi Akiva’s questions to Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua in the meat market of Emmaus (the sister who is also an aunt, the dangling limb, five offerings slaughtered outside or eaten as notar), Rabbi Eliezer on repeated acts, and a baraita on notar from one offering in five pots.
topics: 🐑 Sumakhos’s eighty lashes and Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri’s mother-in-law: differentiated names or differentiated bodies?
🛒 Rabbi Akiva’s question in the meat market of Emmaus: one woman who is his sister, his father’s sister and his mother’s sister
📜 “He has uncovered his sister’s nakedness” and Rav Adda bar Ahava’s case
🔁 Rabbi Eliezer on repeated acts: “he did two” or “they cannot be combined”? Rabba, Rav Yosef, and the vine trellised over a fig tree
🩹 The dangling limb and the people afflicted with boils on Passover eve; the leek, the rain and “removed with great force”
🔪 Five offerings slaughtered outside, or notar from five offerings? Rabbi Shimon’s version and Rabbi Akiva’s response
🍲 One offering in five pots: notar, misuse, and provisional guilt offerings

a1.he: שְׁחָטָהּ וְאֶת בַּת בִּתָּהּ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ שָׁחַט אֶת בִּתָּהּ – סוֹפֵג אֶת הָאַרְבָּעִים. סוֹמְכוֹס אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר: סוֹפֵג שְׁמוֹנִים.

a2.he: אָמַר רָבָא: דִּלְמָא לָא הִיא, עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי הָכָא אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם שֵׁמוֹת מוּחְלָקִין, דְּמִיקַּרְיָא חֲמוֹתוֹ, וּמִיקַּרְיָא אֵם חֲמוֹתוֹ, וּמִיקַּרְיָא אֵם חָמִיו.

a3.he: אֲבָל גַּבֵּי אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ, דְּכוּלְּהוּ ״אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ״ מִיקַּרְיָין, דְּאֵין שֵׁמוֹת מוּחְלָקִין – לָא.

a4.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר סוֹמְכוֹס אֶלָּא גַּבֵּי אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ, דְּגוּפִין מוּחְלָקִין.

a5.he: אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּאֵין גּוּפִין מוּחְלָקִין, אֵימָא כְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: ״שַׁאֲרָה הֵנָּה זִמָּה הִיא״, הַכָּתוּב עֲשָׂאָן לְכוּלָּן זִמָּה אַחַת.

a6.he: מַתְנִי׳ אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְאֶת רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בָּאִיטְלֵיס שֶׁל עֵימָאוּם, שֶׁהָלְכוּ לִיקַּח בְּהֵמָה לְמִשְׁתֵּה בְנוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, הַבָּא עַל אֲחוֹתוֹ וְעַל אֲחוֹת אָבִיו וְעַל אֲחוֹת אִמּוֹ, מַהוּ? חַיָּיב אַחַת עַל כּוּלָּן, אוֹ חַיָּיב עַל כָּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת?

a7.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ, אֲבָל שָׁמַעְנוּ: הַבָּא עַל חָמֵשׁ נָשָׁיו נִדּוֹת בְּהֶעְלֵם (אַחַת) [אֶחָד], שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת, (וְרוֹאֶה אֲנִי) [וְרוֹאִין אָנוּ] שֶׁהַדְּבָרִים קַל וָחֹמֶר.

a8.he: גְּמָ׳ הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא כִּדְקָתָנֵי, מַאי תִּיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ? הֲרֵי שֵׁמוֹת מוּחְלָקִין, הֲרֵי גּוּפִין מוּחְלָקִין!

a9.he: אֶלָּא הָכִי קָתָנֵי: הַבָּא עַל אֲחוֹת אָבִיו שֶׁהִיא אֲחוֹת אִמּוֹ, חַיָּיב אַחַת עַל כּוּלָּן, אוֹ חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת, מַהוּ? מִי אָמְרִינַן: הֲרֵי שֵׁמוֹת מוּחְלָקִין, אוֹ דִלְמָא הֲרֵי אֵין גּוּפִין מוּחְלָקִין?

a10.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ, אֲבָל שָׁמַעְנוּ: הַבָּא עַל חָמֵשׁ נָשָׁיו נִדּוֹת בְּבַת אַחַת, שֶׁהוּא שֵׁם אֶחָד, שֶׁחַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת מִשּׁוּם נִדָּה,

a11.he: וְרָאִינוּ שֶׁהַדְּבָרִים קַל וָחוֹמֶר: וּמָה הַבָּא עַל חָמֵשׁ נָשָׁיו נִדּוֹת בְּבַת אַחַת, שֶׁהִיא שֵׁם אַחַת – חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת, אֲחוֹתוֹ שֶׁהִיא אֲחוֹת אָבִיו שֶׁהִיא אֲחוֹת אִמּוֹ, שֶׁהֵן שְׁלֹשָׁה שֵׁמוֹת – אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁיְּהֵא חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת?

a12.he: אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ: מָה לְחָמֵשׁ נִדּוֹת – שֶׁכֵּן גּוּפִין מוּחְלָקִין!

a13.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר קְרָא: ״עֶרְוַת אֲחוֹתוֹ גִלָּה״, לְחַיֵּיב עַל אֲחוֹתוֹ שֶׁהִיא אֲחוֹת אָבִיו שֶׁהִיא אֲחוֹת אִמּוֹ.

a14.he: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ בְּרַשִּׁיעָא בַּר רַשִּׁיעָא, שֶׁבָּא עַל אִמּוֹ וְהוֹלִיד שְׁתֵּי בָּנוֹת, וְחָזַר וּבָא עַל אַחַת מֵהֶן וְהוֹלִיד בֵּן, וּבָא בְּנוֹ עַל אֲחוֹת אִמּוֹ, שֶׁהִיא אֲחוֹתוֹ, שֶׁהִיא אֲחוֹת אָבִיו, דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ רַשִּׁיעָא בַּר רַשִּׁיעָא.

a15.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בָּא עָלֶיהָ, וְחָזַר וּבָא עָלֶיהָ, וְחָזַר וּבָא עָלֶיהָ – חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אֶחָת.

a16.he: וּמוֹדִים חֲכָמִים לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּבָא עַל חָמֵשׁ נָשָׁיו נִדּוֹת בְּבַת אַחַת, שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת, הוֹאִיל וְהוּא גָּרַם לָהֶן.

a17.he: אָמַר רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: מִי אָמְרִינַן ״הוֹאִיל וְהוּא גָּרַם לָהֶן״? וְהָתַנְיָא: הוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם (אַחַת) [אֶחָד] וְהִיא בַּחֲמִשָּׁה הֶעְלֵמוֹת – הוּא אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת וְהִיא חַיֶּיבֶת עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת.

a19.he: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ, קָצַר וְקָצַר – מָה לִי אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר?

a20.he: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם מִשּׁוּם דְּהוּא דַּעֲבַד תַּרְתֵּין, וְאַמְּטוּל (ל)הָכִי אָמַר: חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת, וְהָכָא נָמֵי דַּעֲבַד תַּרְתֵּין,

a21.he: אוֹ דִּלְמָא טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם מִשּׁוּם דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְעָרְבָן לְבִיאוֹת זוֹ בָּזוֹ, אַמְּטוּל (לְ)הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת, אֲבָל קָצַר כִּגְרוֹגֶרֶת וְחָזַר וְקָצַר כִּגְרוֹגֶרֶת בְּהֶעְלֵם (אַחַת) [אֶחָד], כֵּיוָן דְּאֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְעָרֵב שְׁתֵּי גְּרוֹגְרוֹת בְּבַת אַחַת אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אֶחָת, מַאי?

a22.he: אָמַר רַבָּה: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם – מִשּׁוּם דַּעֲבַד תַּרְתֵּי, הָכָא נָמֵי הָא עֲבַד תַּרְתֵּי. וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם – דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְעָרְבָן, אֲבָל אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְעָרְבָן – אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אֶחָת.

a23.he: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַבָּה: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְחַיֵּיב עַל וַלְדֵי מְלָאכוֹת בִּמְקוֹם אֲבוֹת מְלָאכוֹת.

a24.he: הָא אָב וְאָב, בְּבַת אַחַת – פָּטוּר. וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מִשּׁוּם דְּקָעָבֵד תַּרְתֵּי, אַמַּאי פָּטוּר?

a25.he: אָמַר מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּנַן: אֲנָא וְרַב נְחוּמִי בַּר זְכַרְיָה תַּרְגֵּימְנָא: הָכָא בְמַאי עָסְקִינַן –

a26.he: בְּדָלִית הַמּוּדְלֵית עַל גַּבֵּי תְּאֵינָה וּקְצָצָן בְּבַת אַחַת, מִשּׁוּם הָכִי מְחַיֵּיב רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, הוֹאִיל וְשֵׁמוֹת מוּחְלָקִין וְגוּפִין מוּחְלָקִין.

a27.he: דִּכְווֹתַהּ קָצַר וְקָצַר, הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ דְּמִיפְּטַר? כְּגוֹן שֶׁקָּצַר שְׁתֵּי גְּרוֹגְרוֹת בְּבַת אַחַת, אֲבָל קָצַר כִּגְרוֹגֶרֶת וְחָזַר וְקָצַר כִּגְרוֹגֶרֶת – חַיָּיב.

a28.he: מַתְנִי׳ וְעוֹד שָׁאַל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אֵבֶר הַמְדֻולְדָּל בַּבְּהֵמָה, מַהוּ? אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ, אֲבָל שָׁמַעְנוּ אֵבֶר הַמְדֻולְדָּל בָּאָדָם שֶׁהוּא טָהוֹר, וְכָךְ הָיוּ

b1.he: מוּכֵּי שְׁחִין עוֹשִׂין בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם, הוֹלֵךְ לוֹ עֶרֶב פֶּסַח אֵצֶל הָרוֹפֵא, וְחוֹתְכוֹ עַד שֶׁמַּנִּיחַ בּוֹ כְּשַׂעֲרָה, וְתוֹחֲבוֹ בְּסִירָא, וְנִמְשָׁךְ מִמֶּנּוּ,

b2.he: וְהַלָּה, עוֹשֶׂה פִּסְחוֹ וְהָרוֹפֵא עוֹשֶׂה פִּסְחוֹ, וְרוֹאֶה אֲנִי שֶׁהַדְּבָרִים קַל וָחוֹמֶר.

b3.he: גְּמָ׳ תְּנַן הָתָם: הַמּוֹחֵק אֶת הַכְּרֵישָׁה, וְהַסּוֹחֵט בִּשְׂעָרוֹ וּבִכְסוּתוֹ – מַשְׁקִין שֶׁבְּתוֹכוֹ אֵינָם בְּ״כִי יוּתַּן״, וְהַיּוֹצְאִין מִמֶּנּוּ הֲרֵי הֵן בְּ״כִי יוּתַּן״.

b4.he: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: וּכְרֵישָׁה עַצְמָהּ הוּכְשְׁרָה, מַאי טַעְמָא? בִּשְׁעַת פְּרִישָׁה מִמֶּנּוּ הוּכְשְׁרָה.

b5.he: וְהָתְנַן: עֶרֶב פֶּסַח הוֹלֵךְ לוֹ אֵצֶל כּוּ׳. וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁעַת פְּרִישָׁתָן הוּכְשַׁר, הָא אִיכָּא נָמֵי הָהוּא אֵבֶר הַמְדוּלְדָּל, בִּשְׁעַת פְּרִישָׁתוֹ מֵאָדָם – נְטַמְּיֵיהּ לְאָדָם!

b6.he: כִּדְקָאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: בְּנִיתָּזִין בְּכׇל כֹּחָן, הָכָא נָמֵי, בְּנִיתָּזִין בְּכׇל כֹּחָן.

b7.he: וְהֵיכָא אִיתְּמַר דְּרַב יוֹסֵף? אַהָא: זָב וּטְמֵא מֵת שֶׁהָיוּ מְהַלְּכִים וְיָרְדוּ עֲלֵיהֶם גְּשָׁמִים, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁסּוֹחֲטִין זֶה אֶת זֶה, מַשְׁקִין הַיּוֹרְדִין מִצַּד הָעֶלְיוֹן לְצַד הַתַּחְתּוֹן – טְהוֹרִים, שֶׁאֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין אֶלָּא שֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִכּוּלָּן.

b8.he: יָצְאוּ מִכּוּלָּן – הֲרֵי מַכְשִׁירִין, שֶׁאֵין נֶחְשָׁבִין אֶלָּא לְאַחַר שֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִגּוּפוֹ. אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: בְּנִיתָּזִין בְּכׇל כֹּחָן.

b9.he: מַתְנִי׳ וְעוֹד (שָׁאֲלוּ) [שְׁאֵלָן] רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: הַשּׁוֹחֵט חֲמִשָּׁה זְבָחִים בַּחוּץ בְּהֶעְלֵם (אַחַת) [אֶחָד] מַהוּ? חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת, אוֹ אַחַת עַל כּוּלָּן? אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ.

b10.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: שָׁמַעְתִּי בְּאוֹכֵל מִזֶּבַח אֶחָד מֵחֲמִשָּׁה תַּמְחוּיִין בְּהֶעְלֵם אַחַת שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת מִשּׁוּם מְעִילָה, וְרוֹאֶה אֲנִי שֶׁהַדְּבָרִים קַל וָחוֹמֶר.

b11.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: לֹא כָּךְ שָׁאַל(ו) רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, אֶלָּא בְּאוֹכֵל נוֹתָר מֵחֲמִשָּׁה זְבָחִים בְּהֶעְלֵם (אַחַת) [אֶחָד] מַהוּ? חַיָּיב אַחַת עַל כּוּלָּן, אוֹ חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת? אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ.

b12.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: שָׁמַעְתִּי בְּאוֹכֵל מִזֶּבַח אֶחָד בַּחֲמִשָּׁה תַּמְחוּיִין בְּהֶעְלֵם (אַחַת) [אֶחָד] שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת מִשּׁוּם מְעִילָה, וְרוֹאֶה אֲנִי שֶׁהַדְּבָרִים קַל וָחוֹמֶר.

b13.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אִם הֲלָכָה – נְקַבֵּל, אִם לָדִין – יֵשׁ תְּשׁוּבָה. אָמַר לוֹ: הָשֵׁב.

b14.he: אָמַר: וְלֹא אִם אָמַרְתָּ בִּמְעִילָה, שֶׁעָשָׂה בָּהּ אֶת הַמַּאֲכִיל כָּאוֹכֵל וְאֶת הַמְהַנֶּה כַּנֶּהֱנֶה,

b15.he: צֵירֵף אֶת הַמְּעִילָה לִזְמַן מְרוּבֶּה, תֹּאמַר בְּנוֹתָר, שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אַחַת מֵאֵלּוּ.

b16.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן? הָכִי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ: מָה רְאָיָה לְשׁוֹחֵט מֵאוֹכֵל? מָה לְאוֹכֵל שֶׁכֵּן נֶהֱנֶה!

b17.he: אֶלָּא כָּךְ (שָׁאֲלוּ) [שְׁאֵלָן]: הָאוֹכֵל נוֹתָר מֵחֲמִשָּׁה זְבָחִים בְּהֶעְלֵם (אַחַת) [אֶחָד], מַהוּ? חַיָּיב בְּכׇל אַחַת וְאַחַת, אוֹ אַחַת עַל כּוּלָּן? אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ.

b18.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: שָׁמַעְתִּי בְּאוֹכֵל מִזֶּבַח אֶחָד מֵחֲמִשָּׁה תַּמְחוּיִין בְּהֶעְלֵם (אַחַת) [אֶחָד] שֶׁחַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת מִשּׁוּם מְעִילָה, וְרוֹאֶה אֲנִי שֶׁהַדְּבָרִים קַל וָחוֹמֶר – מָה מִזֶּבַח אֶחָד שֶׁאֵין גּוּפִין מוּחְלָקִין חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת מִשּׁוּם תַּמְחוּיִין מוּחְלָקִין, חֲמִשָּׁה זְבָחִים דְּגוּפִין מוּחְלָקִין לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?

b19.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: לֹא כָּךְ שָׁאַל(ו), אֶלָּא בְּאוֹכֵל (מזבח אחד) נוֹתָר מֵחֲמִשָּׁה זְבָחִים בְּהֶעְלֵם (אַחַת) [אֶחָד], מַהוּ? חַיָּיב אַחַת עַל כּוּלָּן, אוֹ חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת? אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ.

b20.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: שָׁמַעְתִּי בְּאוֹכֵל מִזֶּבַח אֶחָד בַּחֲמִשָּׁה תַּמְחוּיִין, שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת מִשּׁוּם מְעִילָה, וְרוֹאֶה אֲנִי שֶׁהַדְּבָרִים קַל וָחוֹמֶר. אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אִם הֲלָכָה נְקַבֵּל כּוּ׳

b21.he: קַיבְּלַהּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְהָא תְּשׁוּבָה מֵרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹ לָא? תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא: אָכַל חָמֵשׁ חֲתִיכוֹת נוֹתָר מִזֶּבַח אֶחָד בְּהֶעְלֵם (אַחַת) [אֶחָד] בַּחֲמִשָּׁה תַּמְחוּיִין – אֵינוֹ מֵבִיא אֶלָּא חַטָּאת אַחַת, וְעַל לֹא הוֹדַע שֶׁלָּהֶן אֵינוֹ מֵבִיא אֶלָּא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי.

b22.he: מֵחֲמִשָּׁה תַּמְחוּיִין בַּחֲמִשָּׁ[ה] הֶעְלֵמוֹת – מֵבִיא חַטָּאת עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת, וְעַל לֹא הוֹדַע שֶׁלָּהֶן מֵבִיא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת. מֵחֲמִשָּׁה זְבָחִים בְּהֶעְלֵם (אַחַת) [אֶחָד] – חַיָּיב.

b23.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ אָכַל חָמֵשׁ חֲתִיכוֹת מֵחֲמִשָּׁה זְבָחִים בְּהֶעְלֵם (אַחַת) [אֶחָד] – אֵינוֹ מֵבִיא אֶלָּא חַטָּאת אֶחָת, וְעַל סְפֵיקָן אֵין מֵבִיא אֶלָּא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי אֶחָד. כְּלָלוֹ שֶׁל דָּבָר: כֹּל שֶׁחֲלוּקִין בְּחַטָּאוֹת – חֲלוּקִין בַּאֲשָׁמוֹת.

b24.he: אָכַל חָמֵשׁ חֲתִיכוֹת בַּחֲמִשָּׁה תַּמְחוּיִין מִזֶּבַח אֶחָד לִפְנֵי זְרִיקַת דָּמִים, אֲפִילּוּ בְּהֶעְלֵם (אַחַת) [אֶחָד] – חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת מִשּׁוּם מְעִילָה.

messages.text: Continued from 14b: Rabbi Elazar, citing Rabbi Hoshaya, said that Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri and Sumakhos said the same thing, and the Gemara began quoting the mishna (Ḥullin 82a) that gives Sumakhos’s ruling.
Gemara

If one slaughtered an animal and its daughter’s daughter and afterward slaughtered the original animal’s daughter, he incurs the forty lashes for transgressing the prohibition against slaughtering an animal and its offspring on a single day (see Leviticus 22:28).

verse.he: וְשׁוֹר אוֹ־שֶׂה אֹתוֹ וְאֶת־בְּנוֹ לֹא תִשְׁחֲטוּ בְּיוֹם אֶחָד׃
verse.en: However, no animal from the herd or from the flock shall be slaughtered on the same day with its young.

notes.he: לא עבד איסורא:
notes.en: He slaughtered it and its daughter’s daughter: [so far] he has committed no transgression.

notes.he: של ראשונה עכשיו נמצא ששחט ב' איסורים ראשונה אותו ואת בנו שלישית ושניה בנו ואותו דבנו שניה ואותו שלישית והילכך סופג פ' לסומכוס אף על גב דשם אחד הן:
notes.en: And afterward slaughtered its daughter: [the daughter] of the first. Now it turns out that he slaughtered [her] with two prohibitions: [with] the first [animal], “it and its offspring,” [the first being the mother and] the third [its offspring]; and [with] the second, “its offspring and it,” for its offspring is the second and “it” is the third. Therefore he incurs eighty [lashes] according to Sumakhos, even though they are one name.

messages.text: He incurs eighty lashes for slaughtering the third animal, as its mother and its daughter had already been slaughtered on that day.

notes.he: סופג שמונים אחד משום היא ובתה ואחד משום בתה ואותה דמה לי היא ובתה ומה לי בתה ואותה וחייב שתים ות"ק דאמר ארבעים קסבר שם אחד הן:
notes.en: [Printed note: up to here belongs to 14b.] Sumakhos says: he incurs eighty: one because of “it and its daughter” and one because of “its daughter and it,” for what difference is it to me whether it is “it and its daughter” or “its daughter and it”; so he is liable two. And the first tanna, who says forty, holds that they are one name.

messages.text: This indicates that Sumakhos also maintains that when a person commits a single act and thereby commits two transgressions that are derived from a single verse, he is liable to receive punishment for both violations.
Perhaps it is not so, as Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri would not agree with the ruling of Sumakhos.

It is possible that Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri says that one is liable to bring multiple sin offerings only here, in the case of one who engaged in intercourse with his mother-in-law, only due to the differentiated names of the prohibitions, as she is called his mother-in-law, and she is called his mother-in-law’s mother, and she is called his father-in-law’s mother, and the Torah prohibits each of these relationships separately.

But with regard to the case of slaughtering a mother and its offspring in a single day, where all of the permutations are called: A mother and its offspring, as there are no differentiated names given in the Torah for slaughtering a mother animal and then its offspring or for slaughtering the offspring and subsequently its mother, Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri might maintain that one is not liable to receive multiple sets of lashes.

Perhaps Sumakhos says that one is liable to receive two sets of lashes only with regard to the case of slaughtering a mother and its offspring on the same day, as there are differentiated bodies. Although he violated the same prohibition twice, he did so by slaughtering three different animals.

notes.he: שמחמת ראשונה ושניה באו אלו שני איסורים על השלישית אבל הכא אין גופין מוחלקין:
notes.en: Differentiated bodies: for it is because of the first and the second [animals] that these two prohibitions came upon the third. But here the bodies are not differentiated.

notes.dh: עד כאן לא קאמר סומכוס אלא באותו ואת בנו דגופין מוחלקין
notes.he: ולענין אחות אשה נמי אם היה נשוי ב' נשים ובא על השלישית שהיא אחות שתיהן זו מצד אם וזו מצד אב סומכוס מחייב [על] שתיהן:
notes.en: Sumakhos says this only with regard to a mother and its offspring, where the bodies are differentiated: and with regard to a wife’s sister too, if he was married to two women and engaged in intercourse with a third who is the sister of both of them, of this one on the mother’s side and of that one on the father’s side, Sumakhos deems him liable for both.

messages.text: But here, with regard to a mother-in-law, where there are not several differentiated bodies, as the man engaged in intercourse with only one woman, one might say that Sumakhos holds in accordance with the statement that Rabbi Abbahu says in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan,

notes.he: אבל הכא אע"ג דעל ידי בתה ובת בתה ובת בנה נאסרה הזקנה עליו ג' איסורים ואין גופין מוחלקין בה:
notes.en: Perhaps like Rabbi Abbahu: but here, even though it is through her daughter, her daughter’s daughter and her son’s daughter that the elder woman became forbidden to him by three prohibitions, there are no differentiated bodies in her.

notes.he: משום דגופין מוחלקין דג' בהמות שחט ועבר תרי איסורי אבל הבא על חמותו דאין גופין מוחלקין כרבי אבהו סבירא ליה דאינו חייב אלא אחת דאמר אשה ובתה את בת בנה ואת בת בתה שארה הנה זמה היא הכתוב עשאן לכולן זימה אחת הואיל וכולן יש להן שם בת אשתו. וכ"ש בחמותו דהויא שם אחד וגוף אחד:
notes.en: Because the bodies are differentiated: for he slaughtered three animals and violated two prohibitions. But [in the case of] one who engages in intercourse with his mother-in-law, where the bodies are not differentiated, he holds like Rabbi Abbahu, that he is liable only one; [Rabbi Abbahu] said: “a woman and her daughter… her son’s daughter and her daughter’s daughter… they are near kinswomen; it is lewdness”: the verse rendered them all one lewdness, since all of them bear the name of his wife’s daughter. All the more so with his mother-in-law, which is one name and one body.

messages.text: The verse that introduces the prohibitions against engaging in intercourse with one’s mother-in-law, one’s mother-in-law’s mother, and one’s father-in-law’s mother concludes with the phrase: “They are near kinswomen; it is lewdness” (Leviticus 18:17). This teaches that although these are different relationships, the verse rendered them all one single prohibition of lewdness, for which only a single sin offering is brought.
messages.lead: as Rabbi Abbahu says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says:

verse.he: עֶרְוַת אִשָּׁה וּבִתָּהּ לֹא תְגַלֵּה אֶת־בַּת־בְּנָהּ וְאֶת־בַּת־בִּתָּהּ לֹא תִקַּח לְגַלּוֹת עֶרְוָתָהּ שַׁאֲרָה הֵנָּה זִמָּה הִוא׃
verse.en: Do not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter; nor shall you take to wife her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter and uncover her nakedness: they are kindred; it is depravity.

notes.he: דאינו חייב על אשה ובתה ובת בתה ובת בנה בביאה אחת כמתני' אלא אחת והיינו חמותו ואם חמותו ואם חמיו:
notes.en: One lewdness: that he is liable only one [offering] for a woman, her daughter, her daughter’s daughter and her son’s daughter in one act of intercourse, as in our mishna; and these are his mother-in-law, his mother-in-law’s mother and his father-in-law’s mother.

messages.text: Mishna
I asked Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua in the meat market [itlis] in Emmaus, where they went to purchase an animal for the wedding feast of the son of Rabban Gamliel:

notes.he: שוק:
notes.en: Mishna. In the itlis: the market.

notes.he: שם העיר:
notes.en: Emmaus: the name of the town.

notes.he: להודיע שבחן שאע"פ שהיו טרודין היו עוסקין בדברי תורה:
notes.en: Who went to purchase an animal for the feast, etc.: [this is told] to make known their praise, that even though they were busy, they were occupied with words of Torah.

messages.text: In the case of one who unwittingly engages in intercourse with his sister, and the sister of his father, and the sister of his mother, during one lapse of awareness, what is the halakha? Is he liable to bring one sin offering for all three prohibitions, or is he liable to bring a separate sin offering for each and every one of the prohibitions?

notes.he: מפרש בגמ':
notes.en: One who engages in intercourse with his sister, etc.: it is explained in the Gemara.

notes.he: משום דשם אחות אחת היא:
notes.en: What is it: is he liable one for all of them? Because it is one name of sister.

notes.dh: או חייב על כל אחת ואחת
notes.he: דהויין גופין מוחלקין:
notes.en: Or is he liable for each and every one? Since they are differentiated bodies.

messages.text: @Rabbi Akiva We did not hear a ruling from our teachers about that case, but we heard the following ruling: One who engages in intercourse with each of his five wives while they are menstruating, during one lapse of awareness, we heard that he is liable to bring a separate sin offering for having engaged in intercourse with each and every one of them.

And it appears to me that these matters can be derived from an a fortiori inference: If he is liable to bring separate sin offerings for having engaged in intercourse with five menstruating women, who are forbidden by one prohibition, he should certainly be liable to bring separate sin offerings for having engaged in intercourse with his sister, the sister of his father, and the sister of his mother, who are forbidden by three separate prohibitions.

notes.dh: אמרו לו לא שמענו אבל כו'
notes.he: ורואים אנו שהדברים ק"ו. מפרש בגמרא:
notes.en: They said to him: we did not hear, but, etc. And we see that the matters are a fortiori: it is explained in the Gemara.

messages.text: Gemara

What are the circumstances about which Rabbi Akiva inquired? If we say that the circumstances are precisely as the mishna teaches them, that one unwittingly engaged in intercourse with his sister, and the sister of his father, and the sister of his mother, then for what purpose did Rabbi Akiva raise this dilemma before Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua?
messages.lead: The Gemara raises a difficulty with regard to Rabbi Akiva’s question:
messages.quote: one who engages in intercourse with his sister, and the sister of his father, and the sister of his mother

notes.he: על אחותו ועל אחות אביו ועל אחות אמו אמאי קא בעי אי חייב אחת על כולן הרי שמות מוחלקין וגופין מוחלקין:
notes.en: If we say it is as it teaches: [one who engages in intercourse] with his sister, with his father’s sister and with his mother’s sister, why does he ask whether he is liable one for all of them? They are differentiated names and differentiated bodies.

messages.text: Aren’t they differentiated names of prohibitions and aren’t they also differentiated bodies? Since the man engaged in intercourse with three women, who are forbidden by three distinct prohibitions, it is obvious that he is obligated to bring three separate sin offerings.

notes.he: שג' לאוין מוחלקין בהו:
notes.en: Gemara. Aren’t they differentiated names: for three distinct prohibitions apply to them.

notes.he: לאוין:
notes.en: Names: [meaning] prohibitions.

notes.he: ואף על גב דלעיל גבי עריות צריך קרא אשה לחייב על כל אשה ואשה אף על גב דגופין מוחלקין מ"מ הוה פשיטא ליה לרבי עקיבא דגופין מוחלקין חייב על כל אחת ואחת:
notes.en: Aren’t they differentiated names: and even though above, with regard to forbidden relations, the verse “a woman” is needed to make him liable for each woman even though the bodies are differentiated, nevertheless it was obvious to Rabbi Akiva that where the bodies are differentiated he is liable for each one.

messages.text: Rather, it must be that this is what the mishna is teaching:

In the case of one who unwittingly engages in intercourse with his sister who is also the sister of his father and who is also the sister of his mother, is he liable to bring only one sin offering for violating all of those prohibitions, or is he liable to bring a separate sin offering for each and every one? What is the halakha?

Do we say that they are differentiated names of prohibitions, and since he violated distinct prohibitions, he is liable to bring separate sin offerings? Or perhaps we say: It is not a case of differentiated bodies; since he engaged in intercourse with only one woman, he is liable to bring only a single sin offering.

messages.alt: and Rabbi Yehoshua, as the Gemara restates it
messages.text: @Rabbi Akiva We did not hear a ruling from our teachers about that case, but we heard the following ruling: With regard to one who engages in intercourse with each of his five wives while they are menstruating, at the same time, i.e., during one lapse of awareness, which is five instances of violating one category of prohibition, we heard that he is liable to bring a separate sin offering for having engaged in intercourse with each and every one of them, due to the prohibition against engaging in intercourse with a menstruating woman.
messages.lead: And in response, they said to him:

messages.alt: and Rabbi Yehoshua, as the Gemara restates it
messages.text: And it appears to us that these matters can be derived from an a fortiori inference: If one who engages in intercourse with his five wives while they are menstruating, at the same time, which is only one name of a prohibition, is nevertheless liable to bring a sin offering for each and every one of them, then in the case of one who engages in intercourse with his sister who is also the sister of his father and the sister of his mother, which are three separate prohibition names, is it not logical that he should be liable for each and every one of them?

notes.he: לנדה לא תקרב:
notes.en: One name: [the prohibition] for a menstruating woman, “you shall not approach.”

notes.he: כדמפרש לקמי' ברשיעא בר רשיעא:
notes.en: Who is his father’s sister: as explained below, with “a wicked man, the son of a wicked man.”

messages.text: This line of reasoning can be refuted, as follows: What is notable about the case of five menstruating women that would render one liable to bring a separate sin offering for having intercourse with each one of them? It is notable in that they are differentiated bodies, which is not the case with regard to one’s sister who is also the sister of his father and the sister of his mother, as she is a single person.
messages.quote: If one who engages in intercourse with his five wives while they are menstruating

notes.dh: איכא למיפרך מה לה' נשיו כו'
notes.he: ר"ג ור' יהושע דעבדי הק"ו סבירא ליה דלא תליא מילתא אלא בשמות:
notes.en: This can be refuted: what about five wives, etc.: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua, who made the a fortiori inference, hold that the matter depends only on the names.

messages.text: Rather, the reason one is liable to bring three separate sin offerings for engaging in intercourse with his sister who is also the sister of his mother and the sister of his father is that the verse states: “And if a man takes his sister…and they shall be cut off [venikhretu] in the sight of the children of their people; he has uncovered his sister’s nakedness” (Leviticus 20:17).

verse.he: וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יִקַּח אֶת־אֲחֹתוֹ בַּת־אָבִיו אוֹ בַת־אִמּוֹ וְרָאָה אֶת־עֶרְוָתָהּ וְהִיא־תִרְאֶה אֶת־עֶרְוָתוֹ חֶסֶד הוּא וְנִכְרְתוּ לְעֵינֵי בְּנֵי עַמָּם עֶרְוַת אֲחֹתוֹ גִּלָּה עֲוֺנוֹ יִשָּׂא׃
verse.en: If a man marries his sister, the daughter of either his father or his mother, so that he sees her nakedness and she sees his nakedness, it is a disgrace; they shall be excommunicated in the sight of their kinsfolk. He has uncovered the nakedness of his sister, he shall bear the guilt.

notes.he: מפרש בפ"ק (לעיל כריתות ב:) דאייתר ליה להא דרשא:
notes.en: He has uncovered his sister’s nakedness: it is explained in the first chapter (above, Keritot 2b) that this [phrase] is left over for him for this exposition.

notes.he: הקשה רבינו ברוך אמאי לא מייתי כרת דכתיב באחותו דמצרכי רבנן להכי ומייתי לדרבי יצחק ויש לומר דמייתי הא דפשוט יותר וכהאי גוונא אשכחנא בסנהדרין (דף לד:) ובמגילה (דף כ.):
notes.en: He has uncovered his sister’s nakedness: Rabbeinu Barukh asked: why does [the Gemara] not cite the karet that is written with regard to his sister, which the Rabbis need for this, and instead cites that of Rabbi Yitzḥak? One can say that it cites the one that is plainer. We find the like in Sanhedrin (34b) and in Megilla (20a).

messages.text: The final clause in this verse serves to render him liable to receive three separate penalties of karet for intentional intercourse, or to bring three separate sin offerings for unwitting intercourse, with his sister who is also the sister of his father and who is the sister of his mother.

notes.he: אין להקשות מנ"ל לאוקמא בכה"ג דשלשתן שם אחוה אחת אימא דמיירי במחולקין לגמרי כגון בת בתו וכלתו דהא קרא באחוה מיירי אך קשה איסור כולל ומוסיף מנא ליה דהכא איסור בת אחת היא:
notes.en: To render him liable for his sister, etc.: one should not ask how [the Gemara] knows to set it in such a case, where all three are one sister; say that it speaks of entirely separate women, such as his daughter’s daughter and his daughter-in-law. [One should not ask this,] for the verse speaks of sisterhood. But it is difficult: [as for the rules of] a comprehensive or an added prohibition, how does he know that here it is a prohibition [that takes effect] all at once?

notes.he: אלא מצי מהדרי ליה מאחותו דסיפא דאיש אשר יקח את אחותו דיתירא הוא לחייב על אחותו שהיא אחות אביו ושהיא אחות אמו לחייבו על כל שם ושם:
notes.en: Rather, they could answer him from “his sister” at the end of [the verse] “a man who takes his sister,” which is superfluous: to make him liable for his sister who is his father’s sister and who is his mother’s sister, making him liable for each name.

messages.text: You find it in the case of a wicked man, the son of a wicked man. The case applies if a man engaged in intercourse with his mother and fathered two daughters, and then engaged in intercourse with one of those daughters and fathered a son, and his son engaged in intercourse with his mother’s sister who is also his own sister, because they share a father, and who is also his father’s sister.
messages.lead: The Gemara explains how there could be a case where one’s sister is also the sister of his father and the sister of his mother:

notes.he: ומשכחת לה כו':
notes.en: And you find it, etc.

messages.text: This individual is a wicked man, the son of a wicked man, as both he and his father engaged in incestuous relationships.

If one unwittingly engages in intercourse with a woman who is forbidden to him under the penalty of excision from the World-to-Come [karet], and then again engages in intercourse with her, and then yet again engages in intercourse with her, all during one lapse of awareness, he is liable to bring a separate sin offering for each and every one of the acts of intercourse with her. This is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

notes.he: על אחת מכל העריות וחזר ובא עליה בהעלם אחת:
notes.en: He engaged in intercourse with her: with one of all the forbidden women, and again engaged in intercourse with her, during one lapse of awareness.

messages.text: He is liable to bring only one sin offering.

And the Rabbis concede to Rabbi Eliezer with regard to one who engages in intercourse with his five wives while they are menstruating, where the prohibition was violated unwittingly by both the man and the woman, at the same time, i.e., during one lapse of awareness, that he is liable for each and every one of them, since he caused each of them to be liable to bring a sin offering.

notes.he: בהעלם אחת:
notes.en: With five menstruating women: during one lapse of awareness.

notes.he: להביא כל אחת חטאת דהיינו ה' חטאות הלכך הוא נמי מייתי ה' חטאות אבל ה' ביאות בערוה אחת בהעלם א' היא נמי לא מתיא אלא חד וכן הוא:
notes.en: Since he caused them: each one to bring a sin offering, that is, five sin offerings; therefore he too brings five sin offerings. But [for] five acts of intercourse with one forbidden woman during one lapse of awareness, she too brings only one, and so does he.

notes.he: בא עליה על אחת מכל העריות וחזר ובא עליה והואיל והוא גרם להן שהן חייבות קרבן על כל אחת ואחת אף הוא חייב קרבן על כל אחת ואחת:
notes.en: He engaged in intercourse with her: with one of all the forbidden women, and again engaged in intercourse with her. And since he caused them to be liable an offering for each one, he too is liable an offering for each one.

messages.text: @Rav Naḥman Do we really say that since he caused each of them to be liable to bring a sin offering, he himself is liable to bring five separate sin offerings? But isn’t it taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: since he caused each of them to be liable to bring a sin offering

messages.text: If one unwittingly engages in intercourse five times with a woman who is forbidden to him, and he does so during one lapse of awareness, without realizing over the course of that time period that the act is forbidden, but she does so during five lapses of awareness, as she repeatedly became aware of the prohibition and then forgot it before the next transgression, he is liable to bring only one sin offering, but she is liable to bring a separate sin offering for each and every one of the five transgressions?

notes.he: בין [בא] ה' ביאות בה' עריות בין ה' ביאות על כל אחת:
notes.en: He during one lapse of awareness: whether he [had] five acts of intercourse with five forbidden women, or five acts of intercourse with each one.

notes.he:
שנודע לכל אחת בין כל ביאה וביאה מביאותיו הוא אינו חייב אלא אחת על כל אחת והיא על כל אחת ואחת חייבת ה' דהיינו על כל ביאה וביאה. אלמא אף על גב דהוא גרם לכל אחת להביא ה' חטאות לא בעי הוא למייתי על כל חדא אלא אחת:
ואית ספרים דכתיב בהו הוא בהעלם אחת והיא בה' העלמות - ובערוה אחת מיירי לשון נקייה הוא ויש"ר כח"ו:
notes.en: And they during five lapses of awareness [Rashi’s text reads “they,” plural, where the printed Gemara reads “she”]: each of them became aware between one act of intercourse and the next. He is liable only one for each one, and each of them is liable five, that is, for every act of intercourse. Evidently, even though he caused each of them to bring five sin offerings, he need not bring more than one for each. Some books read: “he during one lapse of awareness and she during five lapses of awareness,” and [then] it speaks of a single forbidden woman. It is a euphemistic expression. (The printed text ends with an abbreviation, ויש״ר כח״ו, left untranslated.)

notes.he: שבא על אחת מן העריות חמש ביאות בהעלם אחד והיא בחמשה העלמות שהיתה לה ידיעה בין כל אחת ואחת הוא אינו חייב אלא קרבן אחד והיא חייבת על כל אחת ואחת אלמא אע"ג דהוא גרם לה ה' קרבנות דבא עליה ה' ביאות הוא אינו חייב אלא אחת:
notes.en: But isn’t it taught: he during one lapse of awareness: that he engaged in intercourse with one of the forbidden women five times during one lapse of awareness, and she during five lapses of awareness, for she became aware between each one; he is liable only one offering and she is liable for each one. Evidently, even though he caused her five offerings by engaging in intercourse with her five times, he is liable only one.

messages.text: In this case, although he caused her to bring several sin offerings, he himself brings only one sin offering.

Rather, one must say that this is the reason he brings five sin offerings for engaging in intercourse with his five wives while they were each menstruating, during one lapse of awareness: It is because they are differentiated bodies.

notes.he: משום הכי מודו בה' נשיו נדות הואיל וגופין מוחלקין:
notes.en: Rather, say: it is for this reason that they concede in [the case of] his five menstruating wives: since the bodies are differentiated.

messages.text: A dilemma was raised before the Sages: If one reaped a fig-bulk of grain on Shabbat, which is the measure for which one is liable to bring a sin offering, and then reaped another fig-bulk, in a single lapse of awareness, what would Rabbi Eliezer say?
messages.lead: The Gemara discusses the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer that one who repeatedly engages in intercourse with a woman who is forbidden to him is liable to bring a separate sin offering for each act of intercourse, even if this all occurred in a single lapse of awareness.

notes.he: כגרוגרת בשבת וזה השיעור חזר וקצר בהעלם א' מה לי אמר רבי אליעזר:
notes.en: He reaped: a fig-bulk on Shabbat, which is the measure, and again reaped during one lapse of awareness. What would Rabbi Eliezer say to me?

notes.he: בשבת וחזר וקצר כגרוגרות:
notes.en: He reaped a fig-bulk: on Shabbat, and again reaped a fig-bulk.

messages.text: Is the reason for the ruling of Rabbi Eliezer there, with regard to forbidden relations, that the sinner performed two separate prohibited acts, and therefore Rabbi Eliezer says he is liable to bring a separate sin offering for each and every one of the acts? If so, here too, where he performed two separate acts of reaping, he is liable to bring a separate sin offering for each act.

Or, perhaps the reason for the ruling of Rabbi Eliezer there, in the case of forbidden relations, is that it is impossible for the sinner to combine the acts of intercourse with one another, and therefore Rabbi Eliezer says that he is liable to bring a separate sin offering for each and every one of the acts of intercourse.

notes.he: הילכך חשיבי [אבל] קצירת שתי גרוגרות אפשר לערב ולקצור בבת אחת:
notes.en: Two acts of intercourse cannot be combined: therefore they count [as separate]. [But] reaping two fig-bulks can be combined and reaped at the same time.

messages.text: But if one reaped a fig-bulk of grain, and then reaped another fig-bulk, in a single lapse of awareness, since it is possible for him to combine the two fig-bulks of grain together and reap them at the same time, he would be liable to bring only one sin offering. What is the correct explanation for Rabbi Eliezer’s ruling?

notes.dh: מ"ט דר' אליעזר התם בבא עליה וחזר ובא עליה משום דקא עבד תרתין איסורין
notes.he: דהא אי אפשר לערבן לשתי ביאות בבעילה אחת. אבל בקצירה הואיל ויכול לקצור ב' גרוגרות בבת אחת אימא דאינו חייב אלא אחת:
notes.en: What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer there, with one who engaged in intercourse with her and again engaged in intercourse with her? Because he performed two prohibitions, since it is impossible to combine two acts of intercourse into one. But with reaping, since he can reap two fig-bulks at the same time, say that he is liable only one.

messages.text: The reason for the ruling of Rabbi Eliezer there, in the case of forbidden relations, is that the sinner performed two separate prohibited acts; and here too, he has performed two separate acts of reaping and is liable to bring two sin offerings.

The reason for the ruling of Rabbi Eliezer there, in the case of forbidden relations, is that it is impossible for him to combine the two transgressions into a single act; but if it is possible for him to combine them, e.g., by reaping two fig-bulks of grain, he is liable to bring only one sin offering.

Each type of labor prohibited on Shabbat comprises acts that are primary categories of that labor and acts that are subcategories of that labor, both prohibited by Torah law. Rabbi Eliezer deems one liable to bring separate sin offerings for the performance of subcategories of prohibited labor on Shabbat in a situation where he also performed the corresponding primary categories of prohibited labor during the same lapse of awareness. For example, if one planted grain on Shabbat and then watered the field, which is a subcategory of the prohibited labor of planting, he is liable to bring two sin offerings.
messages.lead: Abaye raised an objection to the opinion of Rabba from a baraita:
messages.quote: here too, he has performed two separate acts of reaping

notes.dh: ר' אליעזר מחייב על ולדי מלאכות במקום אבות מלאכות
notes.he: שאם עשה אב ותולדה בהעלם אחת חייב שתים הא אב ואב כגון קצר וקצר דזו וזו אב מלאכה פטור מן אחת:
notes.en: Rabbi Eliezer deems one liable for subcategories of labor in a situation of primary categories of labor: that if he performed a primary category and a subcategory during one lapse of awareness, he is liable two. Hence [for] primary and primary, for example where he reaped and reaped, where each is a primary category of labor, he is exempt from one.

notes.dh: ר' אליעזר מחייב על וולדי מלאכה במקום אבות מלאכה
notes.he: בשעשאן לוולדות עם אבות חייב נמי על הוולדות הואיל והוא מעין אב ולא דמי לאב ממש. והיינו דאמרינן בבא קמא לר' אליעזר דמחייב אתולדה במקום אב היינו הכא. (השוה) [הא] אב ואב כגון שקצר וחזר וקצר פטור ואינו חייב אלא אחת:
notes.en: Rabbi Eliezer deems one liable for subcategories of labor in a situation of primary categories of labor: when he performed the subcategories together with the primaries, he is liable for the subcategories too, since it resembles the primary and is not exactly like the primary. And this is what we say in Bava Kamma, “according to Rabbi Eliezer, who deems one liable for a subcategory in a situation of a primary”: it is this. Hence [for] primary and primary, for example where he reaped and again reaped, he is exempt and is liable only one.

messages.text: It may be inferred from this statement that: But if one performed a primary category of labor and then performed the same primary category at the same time, i.e., during the same lapse of awareness, he is exempt from bringing a second sin offering.

But if you say that the reason for the ruling of Rabbi Eliezer in the case of one who engages in repeated acts of intercourse with a woman forbidden to him is because the sinner performed two separate prohibited acts, then why is one exempt from bringing a second sin offering for repeatedly performing a primary category of prohibited labor on Shabbat, when he too has performed distinct prohibited acts?

Rav Naḥumi bar Zekharya and I interpreted the baraita as follows: What are we dealing with here, in the case where one is liable to bring two sin offerings for performing a primary category of prohibited labor and its subcategory?

notes.he: הא דקתני רבי אליעזר כו' דדייקינן מינה הא אב ואב פטור:
notes.en: What are we dealing with here: in what Rabbi Eliezer taught, etc., from which we inferred that [for] primary and primary he is exempt.

messages.text: It is a case of a climbing grapevine that is trellised over a fig tree, and he cut them both, the grapevine and the figs, at the same time, during one lapse of awareness. Detaching the figs is one of the primary categories of the prohibited labor of harvesting, while pruning the vine in order to use it as fuel for a fire is a subcategory of harvesting.

notes.he: טרייל"א של גפן היא:
notes.en: A dalit: it is a [climbing] vine (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: ותאנים בתאנה ואין ענבים בגפן והיה צריך לבצור הגפן להסקה וקצץ בבת אחת פרי התאנה וזמורת הגפן דחייב שתים חדא אפרי דתאנה דהיינו קוצר וחדא אזמורה דתולדה דקוצר דקיימא לן (שבת דף עג:) זומר וצריך לעצים תולדה דקוצר היא משום הכי חייב שתים אף על גב דבבת אחת הואיל ושמות מוחלקין זה אב וזו תולדה וגופין מוחלקין דשני אילנות הן:
notes.en: Trellised over a fig tree: and there were figs on the fig tree and no grapes on the vine, and he needed to cut the vine for firewood, and he cut the fruit of the fig tree and the branch of the vine at the same time. He is liable two: one for the fruit of the fig tree, which is reaping, and one for the vine branch, which is a subcategory of reaping, as we hold (Shabbat 73b) that one who prunes and needs the wood [performs] a subcategory of reaping. Therefore he is liable two even though [he did it] at the same time, since the names are differentiated, this a primary category and that a subcategory, and the bodies are differentiated, as they are two trees.

messages.text: Due to that reason Rabbi Eliezer deems him liable to bring two sin offerings, since it is a case of differentiated names of prohibitions, as he violated both the primary category of the labor and a subcategory, and it is also a case of differentiated physical entities, as he detached figs and part of a grapevine.

notes.he: הכא במאי עסקינן באי זו תולדה במקום אב קא מחייב בדלית המודלת על גבי תאינה וקצץ האשכול והתאינה בבת אחת דמשום הכי מיחייב דתרי מינין נינהו ובצירה היינו אב ולקיטה דתאינה היינו תולדה. ומ"ט הוי בצירה אב מלאכה הא לא כתיבא בחשבון אבות מלאכות כיון דכתיב בצירה וקצירה בחד קרא את ספיח קצירך לא תקצור ואת ענבי נזירך לא תבצור אלמא תרווייהו הוויין אבות מלאכות:
notes.en: What are we dealing with here: in which subcategory in a situation of a primary does he deem one liable? A climbing vine trellised over a fig tree, where he cut the cluster and the fig at the same time; that is why he is liable, for they are two kinds: harvesting grapes is the primary, and gathering the fig is the subcategory. And why is harvesting grapes a primary category of labor, when it is not written in the count of primary labors? Since harvesting grapes and reaping are written in one verse, “That which grows of itself of your harvest you shall not reap, and the grapes of your undressed vine you shall not gather,” evidently both are primary categories of labor.

messages.text: In the corresponding situation, where one reaped a fig-bulk of grain on Shabbat and then reaped another fig-bulk in a single lapse of awareness, how can you find circumstances in which he is exempt from bringing a second sin offering? You find this in a situation where he reaped two fig-bulks simultaneously, in which case he performed only a single prohibited act. But if one reaped a fig-bulk of grain and then reaped another fig-bulk, he is liable to bring two sin offerings, as he performed two separate acts.

notes.he: דדייקינן הא אב ואב פטור כגון שקצר שתי גרוגרות בבת אחת דהשתא לאו תרתין הוא דעבד ובבת אחת עשאן גופין ושמות מוחלקין נמי ליכא אבל קצר וחזר וקצר דתרתין מלאכות עבד בהעלם אחת מחייב ר' אליעזר:
notes.en: Correspondingly, with regard to reaped and reaped: from which we inferred that [for] primary and primary he is exempt, for example where he reaped two fig-bulks at the same time; for then he did not do two [acts], and he did them at the same time, and there are no differentiated bodies or names either. But [if] he reaped and reaped again, where he performed two labors during one lapse of awareness, Rabbi Eliezer deems him liable.

notes.he: דכוותה גבי קצר וקצר דפטר כדקא דייק הא אב ואב בבת אחת פטור כגון שקצר בגרוגרת בבת אחת אבל קצר וחזר וקצר [וחזר] וקצר חייב [על כל אחת ואחת] היינו כדרכה:
notes.en: Correspondingly, with regard to reaped and reaped, where he is exempt, as was inferred: [for] primary and primary at the same time he is exempt, for example where he reaped a fig-bulk at the same time. But [if] he reaped and reaped again [and again] reaped, he is liable [for each one]; that is, [where he did it] in the usual way.

messages.caption: The cases on 15a sorted by the Gemara’s two questions: are the names (prohibitions) differentiated, and are the bodies differentiated? Cells marked “implied” are our reading, not stated in the text.

messages.text: Mishna
What is the status of a dangling limb of an animal? Does it impart ritual impurity like a severed limb?
messages.lead: And furthermore, Rabbi Akiva asked Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua in the meat market of Emmaus:

notes.he: תלוש רובה ומעורה במקצת:
notes.en: Mishna. A dangling limb in an animal: mostly torn off and attached by a little.

notes.he: שיטמא משום אבר מן החי כאילו נתלש לגמרי דקיימא לן בהעור והרוטב (חולין קכח:) דאבר מן החי מטמא כנבלה:
notes.en: What is it: does it impart impurity as a limb from a living creature, as though it had been torn off completely? For we hold in [the chapter] HaOr VeHaRotev (Ḥullin 128b) that a limb from a living creature imparts impurity like a carcass.

notes.he: שפרוש ממנה מקצתו לאוכלו מהן מי מיטמא כאבר הנתלש מן החי אי לא אמרו לו לא שמענו אבל שמענו כו':
notes.en: A dangling limb in an animal: part of which has separated from it; [the question is] whether those who eat of it become impure as with a limb torn from a living creature, or not. They said to him: we did not hear, but we heard, etc.

messages.text: @Rabbi Akiva We have not heard a ruling from our teachers in that specific case, but we have heard with regard to a dangling limb of a person that it is ritually pure. And in this manner would…

notes.he: הנתלש מן האדם לגמרי מטמא כמת בפרק העור והרוטב (חולין קכט:) והמדולדלת שדבוק קצת טהור:
notes.en: A limb: torn off a person completely imparts impurity like a corpse, in [the chapter] HaOr VeHaRotev (Ḥullin 129b); and a dangling one, which is still attached a little, is pure.

notes.he: בפרק העור והרוטב יליף בהמה משרצים ותימה אדם מנ"ל דטהור:
notes.en: A dangling limb in a person is pure: in [the chapter] HaOr VeHaRotev [the Gemara] derives [the law of] an animal from creeping animals. It is puzzling: from where do we know that [the dangling limb of] a person is pure?

notes.he: לא אמר במוכי שחין ממש אלא בכל מכה שמדולדל אבר מחמתה:
notes.en: [Printed note: up to here belongs to 15a.] And so would those afflicted with boils: he did not mean those literally afflicted with boils, but [anyone with] any wound on account of which a limb dangles.

messages.text: …the people afflicted with boils, whose limbs were dangling due to their affliction, act in Jerusalem: Each of them would go on Passover eve to the doctor, who would cut the affected limb almost completely until he would leave it connected by a hairbreadth of flesh, so that neither the doctor nor the afflicted would be rendered ritually impure by a severed limb.

notes.he: אבריהן נופלין:
notes.en: Those afflicted with boils: their limbs fall off.

notes.he: לא משום טהרה שקודם לכן נמי טהור אלא שלא יהא מאוס ברגל באבר המדולדל:
notes.en: And he would cut it: not for the sake of purity, since before this too he is pure, but so that he not be repulsive at the festival with the dangling limb.

notes.he: ולא חותכו לגמרי שלא יטמא אותו החותכו שנוגע בו בשעת פרישה:
notes.en: Until he would leave it like a hair: and he does not cut it off completely, so that the one who cuts it not become impure, for he touches it at the moment of separation.

messages.text: Then, the doctor would impale the limb on a thorn attached to the floor or the wall, and the afflicted would pull away from the thorn, thereby completely severing the limb.

notes.he: לאבר בסירא בקוץ המחובר לקרקע או לכותל והוא החולה נמשך ונתלש האבר מאליו:
notes.en: And impale it: the limb, on a thorn attached to the ground or to the wall; and he, the sick man, would pull away, and the limb would be torn off by itself.

notes.he: הולך לו ערב פסחים אצל הרופא וחותכו הרופא לאותו אבר המדולדל עד שמניח בו כחוט השערה דבוק בגוף ותוחבו לאותו אבר המדולדל ונועצו בארץ עם האבר המדולדל ונמשך הימנו בעל האבר והיה נתלש החוט ונשתייר שם האבר והלה שהיה בעל האבר עושה פסחו בטהרה שכבר נפסק ממנו אבר המדולדל. ואפילו קודם שנפסק היה טהור לעשות פסח כדאמר שאבר המדולדל באדם טהור אלא רבותא קמ"ל דאפי' כי חתכו ופסקו בזה הענין טהור הרופא ובעל האבר דלא טמייה אבר לאבר בשעת פרישתו ממנו דמוקמינן בגמרא דבניתזין בכל כחו שעקרו לאותו חוט בכח במהרה דלא שהה כלל שיטמאנו:
notes.en: [Each] would go on Passover eve to the doctor, and the doctor would cut that dangling limb until he left a hairbreadth of it attached to the body, and he would impale that dangling limb, fixing it in the ground with the dangling limb [on it]; and the owner of the limb would pull away from it, the hair[breadth] would be torn, and the limb would remain there. And that [man], the owner of the limb, would perform his Paschal offering in purity, since the dangling limb had already been cut off from him. And even before it was cut off he was pure to perform the Paschal offering, as it says that a dangling limb in a person is pure; but it teaches us something more: that even when he cut it and severed it in this way, the doctor and the owner of the limb are pure, for the limb did not render him impure at the moment it separated from him. For we establish in the Gemara that it is [a case] where they are removed with all their force: he tore that hair[breadth] away forcefully and quickly, so that it did not linger at all to render him impure.

messages.text: And that person afflicted with boils would perform the rite of his Paschal offering, and the doctor would perform the rite of his Paschal offering, as neither had come into contact with the limb once it was severed. In any case, as long as it was dangling, the limb did not impart impurity.

And I consider that these matters can be derived from an a fortiori inference. If a person’s limb, the impurity of which when amputated is severe, does not impart impurity when it is dangling, it is all the more so logical that an animal’s limb, the impurity of which when amputated is lenient, does not impart impurity when it is dangling.

notes.he: מפרש בגמ' אדם שמטמא מחיים שמקבל טומאה מחיים [ואפילו הכי לא מטמא אבר המדולדל ק"ו בהמה שאינה מקבלת טומאה מחיים]:
notes.en: A fortiori: it is explained in the Gemara: [if] a person, who imparts impurity while alive, [and] who receives impurity while alive, [even so his dangling limb does not impart impurity, all the more so an animal, which does not receive impurity while alive].

notes.he: מפרש בגמרא מאי ק"ו:
notes.en: And we see that the matters are a fortiori: the Gemara explains what the a fortiori is.

notes.he: ומה אדם שמטמא מחיים זב ובטמא מת:
notes.en: Just as a person, who imparts impurity while alive: [as] a zav and one impure from a corpse.

messages.text: Gemara
We learned in a mishna elsewhere (Makhshirin 1:5):

With regard to one who forcefully wipes rainwater from the surface of a leek or squeezes out water absorbed in his hair or in his clothing, the liquid that remains within it is not included under the rubric of the verse: “If water be put upon the seed, and some of their carcass fall on it, it is impure for you” (Leviticus 11:38). Therefore, it cannot render food susceptible to contracting ritual impurity.

verse.he: וְכִי יֻתַּן־מַיִם עַל־זֶרַע וְנָפַל מִנִּבְלָתָם עָלָיו טָמֵא הוּא לָכֶם׃ {ס}
verse.en: but if water is put on the seed and any part of a carcass falls upon it, it shall be impure for you.

notes.he: כותש את הקפלוט שקורין פור"ש:
notes.en: Gemara. One who wipes the leek: who crushes the leek [kaflut], which is called (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: כגון יוצא מבית המרחץ ומסתפג באלונטית:
notes.en: One who squeezes out water in his hair: for example, one who comes out of the bathhouse and dries himself with a towel.

notes.he: שבתוך הכרישה אינן בכי יותן דלא חשיבי מידי הואיל ובלועין הן:
notes.en: The liquids within it: within the leek are not under “if [water] be put,” for they are of no account, since they are absorbed.

notes.he: פי' בקונטרס כותש הקפלוט וקשה דא"כ פירות נינהו ומי פירות אינן מכשירין ועוד קשה דקאמר הסוחט בשערו אינו בכי יותן והיוצאין ממנו הרי הוא בכי יותן ופי' הקונטרס סחט בשערו אחר שיצא מבית המרחץ וא"כ שבשערו אמאי אינו בכי יותן והלא תחלתו לרצון היה ואמרינן (מכשירין פ"א מ"א) כל משקה שתחלתו לרצון אף על פי שאין סופו לרצון לכך פר"י דמיירי שירדו הגשמים עליהם ולא היה לרצון עד שיצאו מהם:
notes.en: One who wipes the leek: Rashi explained in his commentary: who crushes the leek [kaflut]. This is difficult: if so, these are fruit juices, and fruit juices do not render [food] susceptible. It is further difficult: it says that [the liquid] in his hair, for one who squeezes in his hair, is not under “if [water] be put,” while what comes out of it is under “if [water] be put”; and Rashi explained that he squeezed his hair after coming out of the bathhouse. If so, why is what is in his hair not under “if [water] be put”? Wasn’t it desired at the outset? And we say (Makhshirin 1:1): any liquid that was desired at the outset, even though it is not desired at the end, [renders susceptible]. Therefore the Ri explained that it speaks of rain that fell on them, and it was not desired until it came out of them.

notes.he: פי' רש"י כותש משמע דבעי למימר דבמי שתית הכרישה מיירי ולא נהירא דהא קי"ל דמי פירות אין מכשירין דלא מיקרי משקין ופירש ריב"א מוחק שהחליקו באצבעו או בצפרניו להעביר מי גשמים שעליה דומיא דסוחט בשערו ובכסותו:
notes.en: One who wipes the leek: Rashi explained “crushes,” implying that he means it speaks of the juice from pressing the leek. This is not plausible, for we hold that fruit juices do not render [food] susceptible, as they are not called liquids. And the Riva explained: “wipes,” that he smoothed it with his finger or his nails to remove the rainwater on it, similar to one who squeezes his hair and his garment.

notes.he: חציר כגון שהיתה כרישה מליאה מי גשמים ומוחק באצבעו הגשמים שעל הכרישה שיפלו ממנו וכן הסוחט מי גשמים שבשערו ושבכסותו שיצאו חוץ:
notes.en: One who wipes the leek: grass; for example, a leek that was full of rainwater, and he wipes off with his finger the rain on the leek so that it will fall from it. And likewise one who squeezes the rainwater in his hair and in his garment so that it will come out.

notes.he: המשקין שבתוכו כלומר כל זמן שהמים עליהם המים אינן חשובין משקין להכשיר אם נגעה בהן הטומאה ואינן בכי יותן:
notes.en: The liquids within it: that is, as long as the water is on them, the water does not count as liquid to render [food] susceptible if impurity touches it, and it is not under “if [water] be put.”

messages.text: But the liquid that is released from it, in this process of wiping or squeezing, is included under the rubric of the verse: “If water be put,” and therefore it renders any food it touches susceptible to ritual impurity, as the person has accorded it significance.

notes.dh: והיוצאין הימנו הרי הן בכי יותן
notes.he: אם נפלו על הזרעים:
notes.en: And those released from it are under “if [water] be put”: if they fell on seeds.

notes.dh: והיוצאין ממנו לאחר שיצאו הרי זה בכי יותן
notes.he: אף על גב דשלא ילקה הכותל אינו בכי יותן התם משום דלא ניחא ליה דאתו והכא נמי אף על גב דלא ניחא ליה מעיקרא מכל מקום כיון שהוא עצמו דוחקן להוציא מהם המים אחשבינהו:
notes.en: And those released from it, after they are released, are under “if [water] be put”: even though [water put] so that the wall not be damaged is not under “if [water] be put,” there it is because he does not want it to come. Here too, even though he did not want it at the outset, nevertheless, since he himself presses on it to get the water out of them, he has given it significance.

notes.he: היוצא ממנו מן הכרישה או מן השיער או מן הכסות מאחר שיצאו חשובין משקין להכשיר והרי הן בכי יותן:
notes.en: What is released from it: from the leek, or from the hair or from the garment. Once they have come out, they count as liquids that render [food] susceptible, and they are under “if [water] be put.”

messages.text: And the leek itself is rendered susceptible to ritual impurity. What is the reason for this? The reason is that at the moment of the water’s separation from the leek, the leek is rendered susceptible to ritual impurity by the very water which is released from it.
messages.quote: wipes rainwater from the surface of a leek

notes.he: לאחר שיצאו ממנו המשקין הוכשרה אף על פי שלא נגעה בהן אחר יציאתן:
notes.en: And the leek itself: after the liquids came out of it, it was rendered susceptible, even though it did not touch them after they came out.

notes.he: שנגעה בה הטומאה בעוד שהמים עליה אע"פ שלא הוכשרה בשעת נגיעה הוכשרה בשעה שפרשו ממנה המים דהא אמרינן היוצא ממנו הרי הן בכי יותן:
notes.en: And the leek itself: which impurity touched while the water was on it. Even though it was not rendered susceptible at the time of contact, it was rendered susceptible at the time the water separated from it, for we said that what is released from it is under “if [water] be put.”

messages.text: But we learned in the mishna: A person afflicted with boils would go on Passover eve to the doctor to sever his dangling limb, and the doctor and the afflicted individual would remain pure.
messages.quote: at the moment of the water’s separation from the leek, the leek is rendered susceptible

notes.he: והתנן הולך לו כו':
notes.en: But we learned: he would go, etc.

messages.text: And if you say that at the moment of the water’s separation from the leek, the leek is rendered susceptible to ritual impurity, there is also a parallel situation in that case of the dangling limb; at the moment of its separation from the person with boils it should render that person ritually impure.

notes.he: למוכי שחין:
notes.en: (What is the reason, etc.) It should render the person impure: [the person] afflicted with boils.

messages.text: The explanation is as Rav Yosef says in a different context, that it is referring to a situation where the liquids are removed with great force. Here too, in the case of the dangling limb, it can be explained as referring to a situation where the limbs are removed with great force.

notes.he: שמשך עצמו בכח ונתלש בכח וליכא נגיעה בשעת פרישה אבל מי כרישה יוצאין בנחת ולאחר שיצאו ממנה חשובין הן מיד וקודם שיפלו לארץ נוגעין בה בשעת פרישה:
notes.en: Removed with all their force: that he pulled himself away forcefully and it was torn off forcefully, and there is no contact at the moment of separation. But the leek’s water comes out gently; once it has come out it is immediately of account, and before it falls to the ground it touches [the leek] at the moment of separation.

notes.he: בפרק העור והרוטב לא משני הכי כי פריך טומאת בית הסתרים היא וצ"ל דפלוגתא דאמוראי היא בפרק בהמה המקשה דעולא ורבינא והכא אליבא דרבינא:
notes.en: Removed with all their force: in [the chapter] HaOr VeHaRotev [the Gemara] does not answer this way when it objects that it is impurity of a concealed place. One must say that it is a dispute of amora’im in [the chapter] Behema HaMakshah, between Ulla and Ravina, and here it follows Ravina.

messages.text: Since the limb is pulled off in one powerful motion it is not considered to have touched the person after it was detached. By contrast, the water wiped off the leek is not discharged all at once, and therefore as the drops of water separate from the leek they render it susceptible to ritual impurity.
And where, i.e., in connection to which case, was this explanation of Rav Yosef stated? It was stated with regard to this baraita:

If a man who experiences a gonorrhea-like discharge [zav] and one who is ritually impure through contact with a corpse were walking along and rain fell on them, although they squeeze the garments of one another in order to remove the water, those liquids that flow down from the upper section of a garment to the lower section remain pure. They do not become impure from contact with the impure person or his garments, as these liquids are not considered liquids that can become ritually impure unless they have emerged from those garments entirely.

notes.dh: זב או טמא מת שהיו מהלכין בדרך וירדו גשמים
notes.he: על בגדיהן אף על פי שסחטן הזב בעצמו החליק כסותו כלפי מטה שיפלו המים אותן המשקין היורדין בבגד מלמעלה למטה טהורים ואין מטמאין אדם הנוגע בהן לפי שאינן חשובין הואיל ועומדין ליבלע בשפה התחתונה של בגד:
notes.en: A zav or one impure from a corpse who were walking along the road and rain fell: on their garments. Even though the zav himself squeezed them, [running his hand] down his garment so that the water would fall, those liquids that run down the garment from top to bottom are pure and do not render impure a person who touches them, for they are of no account, since they are destined to be absorbed in the lower hem of the garment.

notes.he: פירש בקונטרס משום שסופה ליבלע בבגד וקשה שהרי במסכת נדה פרק האשה (דף סב: ושם) קאמר חרסין שבלעו משקים טמאים ונפלו לאויר התנור כי הוסק התנור טמא מפני שהמשקין יוצאין ואע"פ שלאחר היסק יחזרו ויבלעו החרסין אלא יש לפרש משום דהוי שלא לרצון כ"ז שהם על בגדיו כמו במשקין שבכרישה:
notes.en: From the upper section to the lower section are pure: Rashi explained in his commentary that it is because it is destined to be absorbed in the garment. This is difficult, for in tractate Nidda, in the chapter HaIsha (62b), it says: earthenware shards that absorbed impure liquids and fell into the airspace of an oven, when the oven is heated it is impure, because the liquids come out, even though after the heating the shards will absorb them again. Rather, one should explain that it is because it is not desired as long as it is on his garments, as with the liquids in the leek.

notes.he: אע"פ שסחטו בגדיהן ויש בהן מים הרבה כל כך שהמים יורדין מצד העליון של בגד לצד התחתון של בגד אעפ"כ טהורין הן המים ולא נטמאו מחמת הזב וטמא מת לפי שאין חשובין משקין לא להכשיר ולא לקבל טומאה אלא לאחר שיצאו מכולן מכל הבגד:
notes.en: Even though they squeezed their garments, and there is so much water in them that the water flows down from the upper side of the garment to the lower side of the garment, even so the water is pure and did not become impure because of the zav and the one impure from a corpse, for it does not count as liquid, either to render susceptible or to receive impurity, until it has emerged from all of it, from the entire garment.

messages.text: Once the liquids have emerged from those garments entirely they render food susceptible to ritual impurity, as the people have accorded it significance by squeezing it out of their garments. But the water itself is still not impure, as it is considered liquid that is susceptible to ritual impurity only after it has completely emerged from the body of those garments.

notes.he: אם נפלו על הזרעים וטהורין שאינן מטמאין את הזרעים אלא אם כן הזב נוגע בהן לאחר שיצאו מכולו. והא דכתיב בסיפא אלא לאחר שיצאו מגופו ל"ג לה:
notes.en: Once they have emerged from all of it, they render susceptible: if they fell on seeds. And they are pure, for they do not render the seeds impure unless the zav touches them after they have emerged from all of it. And what is written in the latter clause, “only after they have emerged from his body,” is not part of our text.

notes.he: וטהורין אלו המים שלא טימאום הבגדים לפי שאין נחשבין משקין אלא לאחר יציאתן:
notes.en: Once they have emerged from all of it, they render susceptible. And this water is pure, for the garments did not render it impure, since it counts as liquid only after it has emerged.

messages.text: The reason the water does not become impure when it separates from the garment is that the baraita is referring to a case where it is removed with great force.

notes.he: אמאי טהורים המים ליטמו מחמת הבגדים בשעת פרישה. לפי שבשעת פרישתן מהן התיזם מהן בכל כחן ולא נשתרו כלל בבגדים ולא טימאום:
notes.en: And Rav Yosef said: why is the water pure? Let it become impure because of the garments at the moment of separation! Because at the moment they separated from them, they spurted from them with all their force and did not remain in the garments at all, so [the garments] did not render them impure.

messages.text: Mishna

With regard to one who unwittingly slaughters five offerings outside the Temple during one lapse of awareness, what is the halakha? Is he liable to bring five sin offerings, one for each and every act of slaughter, or is he liable to bring one sin offering for all the acts of slaughter?
messages.lead: And furthermore, Rabbi Akiva asked Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua:

messages.text: @Rabbi Akiva We have not heard a ruling from our teachers in that specific case.

I have heard with regard to one who eats meat from one offering from five different pots in which they were prepared, during one lapse of awareness, that he is liable to bring five guilt offerings, which are for the meat prepared in each and every pot, due to misuse of consecrated property.

notes.he: משום מעילה על כל תמחוי אם אכלן קודם זריקת דמים:
notes.en: Mishna. He is liable: for misuse, for each pot, if he ate them before the sprinkling of the blood.

messages.text: And I consider that these matters can be derived from an a fortiori inference: If one is liable to bring five guilt offerings for one offering prepared in five pots, all the more so is he liable to bring five sin offerings for slaughtering five offerings outside the Temple.

notes.he: מפרש בגמרא:
notes.en: A fortiori: it is explained in the Gemara.

notes.he: מפרש בגמ' ומה מזבח אחד שאין גופין מוחלקין כו':
notes.en: And we see that the matters are a fortiori: it is explained in the Gemara: just as one offering, where the bodies are not differentiated, etc.

messages.text: It was not that question that Rabbi Akiva asked them. Rather, it was with regard to one who eats notar from five offerings during one lapse of awareness. What is the halakha? Is he liable to bring one sin offering for all the offerings from which he ate notar, or is he liable to bring five sin offerings, one for each and every one of the offerings from which he ate notar?

notes.he: לא דמי לבא על ה' נשיו בהעלם אחת דחייב על כל אחת ואחת לדברי הכל דהנהו יש בהו ב' אזהרות שהוא מוזהר עליה והיא עליו כדלקמן:
notes.en: One who eats notar from five offerings, etc.: this is not like one who engages in intercourse with his five wives during one lapse of awareness, who is liable for each one according to all, for those involve two warnings: he is warned about her and she about him, as below.

messages.alt: and Rabbi Yehoshua, in Rabbi Shimon’s version
messages.text: @Rabbi Akiva We have not heard a ruling from our teachers in that specific case.

I have heard with regard to one who eats meat from one offering that was prepared in five different pots, during one lapse of awareness, that he is liable to bring separate guilt offerings for the meat prepared in each and every pot, due to misuse of consecrated property.

And I consider that these matters can be derived from an a fortiori inference: If one is liable to bring five guilt offerings for one offering prepared in five pots, all the more so is he liable to bring five sin offerings for eating the notar of five separate offerings.

@Rabbi Yehoshua If you are reporting a halakha that you received from your teachers with regard to one who eats notar from five offerings, we will accept it, but if it is based merely on the a fortiori inference from misuse of consecrated property, there is a response that refutes the inference.
messages.quote: And I consider that these matters can be derived from an a fortiori inference

notes.he: שקבלת מרבך שחייב על כל אחד מן הזבחים נקבלנה ממך:
notes.en: If it is a halakha: that you received from your teacher that he is liable for each of the offerings, we will accept it from you.

notes.he: שאתה למד אותה מק"ו ממעילה יש תשובה:
notes.en: And if for inference: that you derive it a fortiori from misuse, there is a response.

notes.he: א"ל ר' עקיבא אם הלכה למשה מסיני היא שחייב על כל אחת ואחת נקבל:
notes.en: Rabbi Akiva said to him: if it is a halakha transmitted to Moses from Sinai that he is liable for each one, we will accept it.

notes.he: כלומר אבל אם אינה הלכה אלא מק"ו אתה רוצה לדון יש תשובה על אותו דין דלא:
notes.en: And if for inference: that is, but if it is not a halakha and you wish to infer it a fortiori, there is a response to that inference, that it is not so.

messages.text: @Rabbi Akiva Respond.

And no; one cannot derive the halakha of notar through an a fortiori inference from misuse of consecrated property: If you said with regard to misuse of consecrated property that one is liable to bring five guilt offerings, perhaps that is because there are additional stringent elements unique to misuse.

As, with regard to misuse, the Torah established that the status of one who feeds another person sacrificial meat is like that of one who eats sacrificial meat, and the status of one who gives benefit to another from consecrated property that is not food is like that of one who derives benefit himself, in that each is liable to bring a guilt offering for misuse.

notes.he: שאם נתן אוכל הקדש לחבירו חייב כאילו אכלה הוא עצמו דקיי"ל המוציא הקדש לחולין הוא מעל ולא מי שניתן לו:
notes.en: One who feeds is like one who eats: that if he gave consecrated food to his fellow, he is liable as though he had eaten it himself; for we hold that the one who takes consecrated property out to non-sacred use is the one who misused it, and not the one to whom it was given.

notes.he: במידי דלאו בר אכילה:
notes.en: And one who gives benefit is like one who derives benefit: with something that is not eaten.

notes.he: והוא הדין דמצי למימר הנהנה כאוכל מה שאין כן בנותר אלא אגב דנקט מאכיל כאוכל קאמר מהנה כנהנה:
notes.en: And one who gives benefit is like one who derives benefit: and the same is true that he could have said that one who derives benefit is like one who eats, which is not so with notar. But since he stated that one who feeds is like one who eats, he states that one who gives benefit is like one who derives benefit.

notes.he: דין הוא שיהא חייב בה על כל אחת ואחת הואיל והחמיר במעילה שעשה בה את המאכיל כאוכל המהנה כנהנה היינו כדאמר במעילה השליח שעשה שליחותו בעל הבית מעל אע"פ דבעה"ב לא אכלו ולא נהנה חייב הוא מעילה כמו שלוחו שאכל ונהנה:
notes.en: If you said with regard to misuse: it is logical that he should be liable for each one there, since [the Torah] was stringent with misuse, making one who feeds like one who eats and one who gives benefit like one who derives benefit. This is as is said in [tractate] Me’ila: [when] the agent carried out his agency, the householder is liable for misuse, even though the householder neither ate it nor benefited, he is liable for misuse just as his agent, who ate and benefited.

messages.text: In addition, the Torah joined the misuse of consecrated property that was performed over an extended period, i.e., if one derived benefit worth half a peruta one day and half a peruta the next, he is liable to bring a guilt offering for misuse. Would you say the same with regard to notar, which has none of these halakhot?

notes.he: שאם נהנה היום בחצי פרוטה ומכאן עד ג' שנים חצי פרוטה מצטרפות לקרבן ולקמן בפרק ספק אכל חלב (כריתות דף יח:) מפיק לה מתמעול מעל ריבה:
notes.en: He joined misuse over an extended period: that if he derived benefit worth half a peruta today, and half a peruta any time from now until three years, they combine for an offering. Below, in the chapter Safek Akhal Ḥelev (Keritot 18b), it derives this from “commit a trespass [timol ma’al],” [a doubled expression that] amplifies.

notes.he: ה"נ המ"ל מאי קא מיבעיא ליה כו' מאחר דר"ע פריך אמילתיה פשיטא דקבלה:
notes.en: He joined misuse, etc.: here too it could have said: what is his dilemma, etc.? Since Rabbi Akiva refutes his statement, it is obvious that he accepted it.

notes.he: אכל קודש שוה פרוטה אחת אפי' בין עשרה ימים מצטרף לפרוטה וחייב מעילה:
notes.en: He joined misuse over an extended period: [if] he ate consecrated food worth one peruta, even across ten days, it combines to a peruta and he is liable for misuse.

notes.he: שאין בו אחד מכל אלו דאין חייב על נותר אלא בכזית בכדי אכילת פרס הילכך אינו דין שיהא חייב על כל אחת ואחת כבמעילה:
notes.en: Would you say with regard to notar, which has none of these: for one is liable for notar only for an olive-bulk [eaten] within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf. Therefore it is not logical that he should be liable for each one, as with misuse.

messages.text: Gemara
What is difficult for Rabbi Shimon with the first version of Rabbi Akiva’s question, that he insists that Rabbi Akiva had asked about one who eats notar from five offerings?
messages.quote: It was not that question that Rabbi Akiva asked them

notes.dh: גמ' מאי קשיא ליה לר' שמעון
notes.he: מה ראייה לשוחט בחוץ מאוכל זבח לפני זריקה:
notes.en: What is difficult for Rabbi Shimon: what proof is there for one who slaughters outside [the Temple] from one who eats of an offering before the sprinkling [of the blood]?

notes.dh: מאי קא קשיא ליה לר' שמעון
notes.he: דאמר לא כך שאלן:
notes.en: What is difficult for Rabbi Shimon, that he said: not so did he ask them?

messages.text: This is what is difficult for him: If Rabbi Akiva asked about one who unwittingly sins by slaughtering, why is the answer derived from an unwitting sin involving eating? After all, what proof can be cited for a case of one who slaughters from a case of one who eats? What is notable about one who eats? It is notable in that he derives benefit from the act of eating, whereas one who slaughters does not derive physical benefit.

notes.he: איהו קא בעי למילף שוחט בחוץ מאוכל דחייב מעילה על כל אחת ואח'. וקא קשיא ליה מה לאוכל דין שהוא חייב על כל אחת ואחת שכן נהנה אבל שוחט אינו נהנה:
notes.en: This is what is difficult for him: he [Rabbi Yehoshua] seeks to derive one who slaughters outside from one who eats, who is liable for misuse for each one. And it is difficult for him: what about one who eats? It is logical that he is liable for each one, since he derives benefit; but one who slaughters does not derive benefit.

messages.text: Rather, he must have asked him this:

In the case of one who eats notar from five offerings during one lapse of awareness, what is the halakha? Is he liable to bring a separate sin offering for each and every one of the offerings, or only one sin offering for all of them?

notes.he: אלא האוכל שאלו האוכל נותר מה' זבחים כו':
notes.en: Rather, he asked them about one who eats notar from five offerings, etc.

messages.alt: and Rabbi Yehoshua, as the Gemara restates it
messages.text: @Rabbi Akiva We have not heard a ruling from our teachers in that specific case.

I have heard with regard to one who eats meat from one offering from five different pots, during one lapse of awareness, that he is liable to bring a separate guilt offering for the meat prepared in each and every pot, due to misuse of consecrated property.

And I consider that these matters may be derived from an a fortiori inference: Just as one who eats from one offering prepared in five pots, in which case the different parts of the offering do not come from differentiated physical entities, is liable to bring a separate guilt offering for the food prepared in each and every pot because he ate from differentiated pots, with regard to one who eats notar from five separate offerings, which are differentiated physical entities, is it not all the more so logical that he is liable to bring a separate sin offering for each and every offering?

§ The mishna teaches that Rabbi Shimon said: It was not that question that Rabbi Akiva asked them. Rather, it was with regard to one who eats notar from five offerings during one lapse of awareness. What is the halakha? Is he liable to bring one sin offering for all the offerings from which he ate notar, or is he liable to bring five sin offerings, one for each and every one of the offerings from which he ate notar? They said to Rabbi Akiva: We have not heard a ruling from our teachers in that specific case.

Rabbi Yehoshua said: I have heard with regard to one who eats meat from one offering from five different pots in which it was prepared, that he is liable to bring a separate guilt offering for the meat prepared in each and every pot, due to misuse of consecrated property. And I consider that these matters may be derived from an a fortiori inference.

Rabbi Akiva said to Rabbi Yehoshua: If you are reporting a halakha that you received from your teachers with regard to one who eats notar from five offerings we will accept it, but if it is based on the a fortiori logical inference from misuse of consecrated property there is a response that refutes the inference.
Did Rabbi Yehoshua accept that refutation from Rabbi Akiva or not?
Come and hear a proof in this regard, as it is taught in a baraita:

If one ate five pieces of notar from one offering during one lapse of awareness, and the pieces were cooked in five different pots, he brings only one sin offering. And in a situation where it is not known to him with certainty whether he unwittingly ate from them, he brings only one provisional guilt offering, which is sacrificed by one who is uncertain whether he committed a sin that renders him liable to bring a sin offering.

notes.he: שהיו ה' חתיכות נותר וה' חתיכות כשרות לפניו ואין ידוע איזו אכל אם הה' של נותר אם הה' כשרות:
notes.en: Not known: that there were five pieces of notar and five permitted pieces before him, and it is not known which he ate, whether the five of notar or the five permitted ones.

messages.text: By contrast, if one ate notar from a single offering from five different pots during five separate lapses of awareness he brings a sin offering for each and every one, and in a situation where it is not known to him with certainty whether he unwittingly ate from them he brings a provisional guilt offering for each and every one.

notes.he: ומזבח אחד אכל נותר חייב ה' משום נותר דהעלמות מחלקין:
notes.en: During five lapses of awareness: and he ate notar from one offering; he is liable five for notar, since lapses of awareness divide.

notes.he: היינו אם ספק לו אם אכל חמש חתיכות נותר בה' תמחוין בה' העלמות צריך להביא חטאת על כל אחת ואחת משום דלדברי הכל ידיעות מחלקות וכן נמי [אם ספק לו אם אכל] אשם תלוי על כל אחת ואחת:
notes.en: And for not being known about them: that is, if he is uncertain whether he ate five pieces of notar in five pots during five lapses of awareness, he must bring a sin offering for each one, since by all opinions awarenesses divide; and so too [if he is uncertain whether he ate, he brings] a provisional guilt offering for each one.

messages.text: If he ate notar from five separate offerings during one lapse of awareness he is liable to bring a separate sin offering for each one, as he ate from differentiated physical entities.

notes.he: אכל נותר בהעלם א' חייב ה' הואיל וגופים מוחלקין. ר' יוסי ור' אליעזר סבירא להו כר' עקיבא דמתני' דר' שמעון:
notes.en: From five offerings: [if] he ate notar during one lapse of awareness, he is liable five, since the bodies are differentiated. Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Eliezer hold in accordance with Rabbi Akiva in the mishna of Rabbi Shimon [so the printed Rashi reads; the baraita here names Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda].

notes.he: מה' זבחים אפי' בהעלם אחד מביא חטאת על כל אחת ואחת ועל לא הודע כו':
notes.en: From five offerings: even during one lapse of awareness he brings a sin offering for each one, and for not being known, etc.

messages.text: Even if he ate five pieces of notar from five separate offerings during one lapse of awareness he brings only one sin offering, as he transgressed one prohibition repeatedly during a single lapse of awareness. And if he is uncertain whether he unwittingly ate from them he brings only a single provisional guilt offering.

The principle of the matter is that in any situation where one’s transgressions are differentiated with regard to sin offerings, i.e., when he is liable to bring multiple sin offerings if he knows that he unwittingly transgressed, they are differentiated with regard to provisional guilt offerings if he is unsure whether he unwittingly transgressed.

notes.he: אתאן לת"ק דאיירי רישא בה' חתיכות נותר מזבח אחד והכי קאמר לגבי מעילה מודינא דתמחויין מחלקין:
notes.en: But if he ate five pieces, etc. [Rashi’s text reads “But”]: we have returned to the first tanna, who spoke in the first clause of five pieces of notar from one offering; and this is what he is saying: with regard to misuse, I concede that pots divide.

messages.text: If one ate five pieces of meat prepared in five separate pots from a single offering before the meat became permitted for consumption through the sprinkling of the blood on the altar, even if this occurred during a single lapse of awareness, he is liable to bring a separate guilt offering for the meat from each and every pot, due to misuse of consecrated property.

notes.he: שייכא מעילה אבל נזרק הדם דהיתה לה שעת היתר לכהנים שוב אין בו מעילה וכן מפורש במנחות בפרק התכלת (מנחות דף מז:):
notes.en: Before the sprinkling of the blood: misuse applies; but once the blood has been sprinkled, since it has had a time of permission for the priests, there is no longer misuse. So it is explained in Menaḥot, in the chapter HaTekhelet (Menaḥot 47b).

notes.dh: כללו של דבר כו' אבל אכל כו'
notes.he: האי אבל אכל ה' חתיכות מזבח אחד בחמשה תמחוין לפני זריקת דמים חייב על כל אחת ואחת משום מעילה דברי הכל היא. והא דקאמר לפני זריקת דמים משום דלאחר זריקה אין בו מעילה שכבר יש בו שעת היתר לכהנים:
notes.en: The principle of the matter, etc. But if he ate, etc.: this [clause], if he ate five pieces from one offering in five pots before the sprinkling of the blood, he is liable for each one due to misuse, is [stated] by all opinions. And it says “before the sprinkling of the blood” because after the sprinkling there is no misuse, for it has already had a time of permission for the priests.

messages.caption: The baraita on notar: what one brings for each case, a sin offering, a provisional guilt offering, or a guilt offering for misuse.

messages.text: Continued on 16a: the Gemara asks whose opinion this baraita follows, to settle whether Rabbi Yehoshua accepted Rabbi Akiva’s refutation.
